MOTHER ROSA GATTORNO

Intimate Diary of mystical experiences

MOTHER ROSA GATTORNO

Foundress of the Daughters of St. Anne

Mother Rosa Gattorno in the 1878. The picture was taken in support of the missionaries leaving for Bolivia, first mission of the Institute

Transcription of Sr. A. Ernestina Degetto, DSA

Introduction and notes of Father Lazaro Iriarte, OFMCap

ROME General House of the Daughters of St. Anne Original Title: Madre Rosa Gattorno.

Memorie - Diario intimo delle esperienze mistiche Translated by Sr. A. Meheret Gombot, DSA Revised by Sr. A. Maria Pinton, DSA

© 9th April 2010

General House of the Daughters of St. Anne

Via Merulana, 177 - 00185 ROMA

Rosa Gattorno was a woman gifted with a rich personality. Her contemporaries admired in her an exceptional human and spiritual wealth and a special way of being and manifesting herself, which, on the one hand, with a strong influence, brought close the hearts of those who were in the sphere of her action and on the other hand, puzzled other men who were used to move within the habitual ascetic, juridical or social tracks. Today, through her writings, published and on their way to publication, we discover in the Foundress that wonderful art of situating herself within a different identity, so to say, in the various areas of her life. No one could say that the woman who, in her thousands of letters shows a surprising sense of reality and an unbelievable ability of government, formation and administration, is the same who at night puts into writing her extraordinary mystical experiences, the same who, having to narrate the history of the Institute, finds a way out through the interlacement of allegoric pictures that constitute the book Travagli e Conforti. If the letters, prove the character of a Foundress who walks with her feet on the ground, and, if in the latter book one discovers the creativity of being an easy-writer who is rich in fantasy, the Memoirs instead offer us the immediate testimony of a secret, divine itinerary of a soul enriched with very uncommon mystical gifts, a soul for which the earthly realities do not count. The center of her life is the supreme Good, the All. But she is always the Foundress who is aware in every moment of her responsibility. In the pages of her Memoirs the events of the Work of God1 are reflected in the way she lives them in her spirit. The reason for which Mother Rosa wrote the Memoirs

The title, willed by her, shows the principal goal of her initiative of putting into writing what God worked in her spirit and the way in which she was experiencing it. These were moments of light and of love which could not be forgotten. Actually, she found special consolation in rereading the notes of the past years and in remembering those experiences, not only to live again the past hours of joy, but also to overcome the moments of trial and the periods of aridity by remembering how she was able to regain peace in such similar situations. In August 1885, after giving her notebooks to be read by her confessor, she wrote:

I am deprived of everything, alone; moreover they have taken away from me even the few scribbles I had. Many times it was of great comfort for me rereading what I wrote in certain moments of aridity and in other states. After it happened I was freed. This was for me of much comfort.

The greatest number of people who write an intimate diary do so in order to find, in this form of journal, a compensation for their loneliness in which they take refuge either because of shyness and also to avoid the superficiality of common relationships. In the case of Rosa Gattorno, we certainly cannot speak of natural shyness but instead she experienced in her own way the weight of solitude in three vital dimensions as the very pages of Memoirs unceasingly testify. First of all, she was feeling “alone without anyone to say a word to” in her interior journey. From the time she Introduction received great infused communications and the first mystical gifts, she was unable to find a spiritual guide who was in tuned with the reality she was living. Though she was convinced of being in dire need for this, she on the other hand, promptly perceived the perplexity of having a confessor at the time when she unveiled herself. For example, no one could approve her programme of physical flagellation, when measuring it by normal ascetic criteria, while she herself had this particular aspect of such unique experience of charismatic origin. She was feeling alone and she repeats it, in the direction of the Work of God, the Institute of the Daughters of Saint Anne, the “spirit” of which she was to be responsible as she was commissioned by Pius IX. Father Tornatore was a valid collaborator for many years but not a confidant. The sisters who were close to her as secretaries or councilors were also useful and very effective collaborators and were convinced of the governing capacity of the Mother; but her governance was distinctly personal. She was: “Alone the midst of such a great Work.” Therefore, she turns to her Good, whose sure guidance fills her with consolation but when He hides himself and leaves her in the most merciless desertion that is the most painful dimension of her solitude. In 1872 she wrote:

Ah! How painful is my present situation! My poor soul, alone, a hermit in the midst of the wide world! She is an orphan and finds herself desolate and immersed in the most bitter tribulations… Now, in the despair of the damned, she finds herself as having lost her Being. I cannot find Him anywhere…

The Memoirs of Mother Rosa, as most intimate diaries are, have no addressee but it is the very intentional absence of an addressee which gives true value of witness to these pages. The Servant of God writes for herself. The only addressee is the paper. Those booklets jealously kept in her secret room are the silent witness of what she describes. In reality however, the true addressee is her Supreme Good to whom she turns now and then with fervent outbursts and acts of love.

As one psychologist wrote, that every author of a diary, however intimate, always thinks (more or less explicitly) to possible readers. Rosa Gattorno is not an exemption. She kept with care all her manuscripts. More than once she refers to these or those -Daughters of Saint Anne- who will read some useful things for their formation.

It was inevitable that sooner or later she had to hand over her notes to a confessor who inspired confidence in her. We know already that before 1873, she had given her notes to a priest so he might read them. Later on, in 1884, she gave some copies of them to be read by Father Bernardino da Portogruaro, Superior General of the Friars Minor, who would cause her then a great suffering. On November 10 of that year she wrote:

I had a heartrending reproach for having given and having said what had passed between me and my dear Crucifix. Oh!

How disgraceful I have been! But weren’t you, my Love, who wanted it that way?

We find similar reactions in the Memorie on the years 1865-1867. On one side Jesus spurs her to write and gives her the strength so that she can write even late at night; on the other hand, the director does not allow her to remain awake. Moreover, she suffered because she had received an order to show her writings with the obligation of writing nothing else but the words of the Lord and of what she barely saw. She found the solution from Jesus Himself: “For him do as he said and for me continue to do as you always do.”

In this way I was very happy, adds the Servant of God. I will take only the words of my God; I will put down nothing else. You my dearest Master, will teach me so that I may obey, because this is truly difficult for me. I find hardship not upon doing it, but only in the duty to disclose the things of my spirit.

This is what she wrote in March 1885. However, this solution of writing two diaries does not seem to have ended the interior tension, keeping in mind that, by temperament Introduction and for evangelical rectitude, Rosa Gattorno was an enemy of any kind of pretence. But when she entrusted herself fully to her great confidant, Msgr. Granito Pignatelli di Belmonte, she had no secrets with him. We see how he himself, being a cardinal, would testify for the process of canonization:

The Servant of God was writing (encouraged by me to continue such writing) – she said - by God’s command, everything that was taking place within her spirit, sorrowful revelations or trials. Now and then, she was giving me some parts to read but she was pleading me strongly not to communicate them to anyone. The fact of showing me these writings was to justify certain permissions she was asking me, since I knew from her writings what took place and, so I was able to regulate.

After the death of the Servant of God her religious sisters, being aware that I had communication of these writings, wanted me to deliver them everything. I reread with attention … (Summarium, p. 5a).

Let it be noted that, while in the years of Father Bernardino da Portogruaro – 1884 to 1887- the notes were decreasing, from the time that the Servant of God started sharing with Monsignor Granito, she was instead filling the pages with more spontaneous news. These were the years of 1888 to1889 and 1890. Afterwards, the letters became every day more confidential and were true spiritual directions. Then the interest in the Memorie diminished. When the wise priest was called to Rome in 1892, at the service of Roman Curia, the spiritual communication with him was mainly verbal. The Memorie, therefore, had no purpose. They diminished in 1893 and were not continued in the following years.

How Mother Rosa wrote her Memorie

Her second autobiographical retrospective journal opens with these words:

Oh! What beautiful and great things you showed me in my contemplations of 1864! I would like to write so many things, but I shall always repeat that, if my Jesus wanted it, he would certainly make me move my pen to his liking; he would give me an angelic promptness, for me to be able to describe what I see and what I feel…

She is convinced that it is God’s will that she writes what she experiences under the superior action. Many times, when she interrupts the taking of notes for lack of time, she feels the reproach of Jesus and so takes anew the pen. Used to move under the light and impulse of the supreme Good, she said that she was writing from his dictation. On May 25, 1891 she said:

I do not know, why with absolute command he orders me to write a certain thing which I do not understand; I only feel that I am writing from dictation. Why this? What is its use? I cannot be silent about the consolation I feel in writing, though as I write I enjoy nothing. Only as I reread the notes, it seems to me that they comfort and support me; moreover they teach much and bring me in conformity to the will of God and in trustful surrender to him.

And on July 2 of the same year:

I have much difficulty in writing certain things. In truth, I should say that I do not understand what I write, and to know what I write I have to stop and reread. ‘Is it me who wrote this?’

  • I ask. Oh! What would God want from this writing or dictation?

I am afraid that it might be a great delusion, but I go repeating within me: the bad monster will have no profit, for by God’s mercy I am able to carry on well my duty and I leave aside nothing… I feel a strong incentive, an interior voice telling me:

‘Go write!’ ‘Yes, my Good!’- I answer – ‘I go!’

Strangely, I take the pen in hand and I do not know about what I should write. I do not have an idea, but always, very soon

I am told and I have no time to construct good sentences, what I have to write comes in so swiftly … When I had to finish, the fountain stops and so I stop.

It is of great help for me reading again what I wrote; the good is always in the holy will of my God. Introduction

The pages of the Memorie do not always gather what the Servant of God is either living at present or what she experienced during the previous days. Many times she repeats a narrative, renewing in her spirit experiences she had two or three months ago. Therefore, the autobiographical reports of the first part of this edition are basically retrospective, though every now and then she includes feelings that she experienced while writing.

The Autobiographical value of the Memorie

Cardinal Granito di Belmonte, in his witness for the process of canonization was able to affirm that the most important aspect of the spirituality of Rosa Gattorno was the one hidden from the eyes of the people, even from the Daughters of Saint Anne who were in direct relationship with the Mother, because it was lived jealously between God and herself. It would have remained hidden, if there were no Memoirs (Summarium, p. 5, 39f).

Without the Memoirs we would fail to get, first of all, the most valuable witness of the deep contemplative experiences of the Servant of God, those hours of absorption in the supreme Good, burning with love, ecstasy, and ineffable communications in the form of visions or other mystical graces. Everything took place in the secret of her room, where she took advantage of the peaceful nights.

Without the Memorie, the variety of the mystical phenomenon, with physical repercussion, would have remained unknown, except some which were confirmed by some sisters to whom the Mother imposed absolute secrecy. Even that which in some way appeared to her, would be ignored in its true cause and constancy, if we had no personal descriptions of it. Nothing, or almost nothing, would be disclosed of the refined planning of fasting, abstinence, physical penance and flagellation of every kind carried out with instruments of her own invention.

More important than these voluntary sufferings, which are true pleasures of her spirit, was the interior torture of feeling alone, “without anyone to say a word to”, having to face all the responsibilities concerning the governance of the Institute in the midst of so much duplicity and pretence which could not escape from her shrewd perception and intuition. In such situations she finds release through the pen as a way of regaining peace. In addition to this, there was the battle sustained especially at night in her room, with the infernal enemy who continually oppressed her with his cunning suggestions, with his monstrous apparitions, uproars, abuses… a battle that reached its highest point when it took the form of despair with the fixation of throwing herself out of the window…

The greatest torment, however, was that of feeling abandoned by God, deprived of his support, like damned… These are the pages that make one creepy with bitterness. These are the well known mystical purifications, a true purgatory in life.

Suffering is an essential component of the life and mission of Rosa Gattorno; it is her way of loving. In the pages of her notes, hours and days of profound consolation are not missing, but each one of these is preceded or followed by inexpressible sufferings, temptations, aridity and pains of hell. She is aware of the painful mark they left in her notebooks. On September 14, 1889, as she took up her diary, she wrote:

I submit myself to write, but I feel pain to fill these pages with every kind of narration, all about pains and tortures of all kinds.

And on May 19, 1892:

It is for long time now that it was not possible for me to write what I feel; I have always my usual strong impulse: ‘Write!’ But my health and the work… I would like to leave out the sufferings

I feel, but how can I if these are my daily food? At night the devils always come in my room in one form or another; with their signs they leave me with upsetting sufferings… Introduction

These fatal signs, which Mother Rosa attributes to the evil one, are presented in the shape of big or small stars that announce the death of a Daughter of Saint Anne; skulls, skeletons and other gloomy figures in the same way predicted the death that took place or soon to take place of priests, Cardinals and even sometimes of Pope Leo XIII.

Key for reading the Memorie

When we approach the autobiographical reports or the descriptions of the intimate experiences of great mystics, first of all we need to have the eyes of faith and participation in the divine in which they see and live the events of their existence and of others; from here comes a habitual discernment and that therefore a perspective of reality, of behavior different from what is common to the majority of people. The centers of interest, the objectives to be achieved and the means to be used are different. Most of all, the light in which they see and judge the events are different. What counts most is that the data of the experience which support their choices does not cohere with the data and calculations which we put into place in the practical life. We need to state precisely some premises for a reading which, on the one hand, does not run the risk of putting into discussion every credibility on the basis of absolute positivism to the bitter end, resorting to pseudoscientific explanation and, on the other hand, keeps present the uneasy border to be maintained between the divine action and the results of the subject’s creativity. 1. The language of the mystics.

More than four centuries ago, Saint John of the Cross had already conducted a theological and psychological analysis of mystical experiences, especially of those which take place on the periphery of the unitive process when the divine invasion on the subject absorbs, but still does not eliminate, the human activity of the exterior and interior senses. There is a need for attention to understand the way of expression of the person who lives such experience under the action of God. In fact, the subject gives shape and figure, sound and words to what he/she is living. The well known warning of the mystical doctor, fruit of his own and others’ experience, is of much importance.

There are spiritual people who, ’with great aptitude form words and reasoning, which to the subject seems it is not he/she who does it all, but another person interiorly suggests him/her the reasoning, the answers and the teachings. In truth he/she reasons with him/herself and answers as if with another person. And, in some way it could be said that it is like that, although it is the human spirit which works, nevertheless it is helped by the Holy

Spirit to produce and formulate those concepts, words and true reasons…’2

Proper to the language of the mystics is the exclusion of any embellished literature, of every covering in view of the effect one wishes to produce in the reader. In the case of the Memoirs of Rosa Gattorno, as we have said that, a hypothetical reader does not exist. She writes as quickly as she speaks, without caring to complete the phrases, entrusting to the pen what she is suggested interiorly. She writes sincerely. One could doubt the objectivity of what she describes, but never its truthfulness. 2. Visions, apprehensions, apparitions…

An accurate study of the manner of expression in the different cases would help us to establish the value of the countless descriptions in the experience of Mother Rosa which succeed in the Memorie. There are real visions, usually accompanied by raptures or by an intense unitive Introduction experience. Other descriptions instead would be numbered among those which the psychologists call “sensory illusions” or “visions in drowsiness” frequent even in normal people.3 The Servant of God places some descriptions and apprehensions at the moment in which she fell asleep. It should be kept in mind that her sleep could never be profound with that body girdled with chain, which every moment gave her terrible spasms, with another chain under the head, lying over a wooden cross, most of the time after a long “discipline until bleeding”.

Among these descriptions, the signs indicated above merit special mention as they sometimes signify the presage of a death of someone, especially of the sisters of the Institute. The Foundress follows passionately all the events of the Work of God, loves each one of her spiritual daughters and accompanies them with painstaking-heart in the places of their work, anxious of their faithfulness to their vocation and of their health. A telepathic disposition, which would make her perceive from afar a danger for a sister or her death, cannot be excluded. The sign of a death was a star, more or less big according the importance of the deceased. But in some months the stars were so many that we find it hard to believe that there were so many deaths in the growing Institute, where most of the sisters were young. 3. The gift of discernment

Saint Paul numbered among the charisms or “particular manifestations of the Spirit for common good,” the gift of discernment of spirits (1 Cor 12: 10). Rosa Gattorno is conscious of possessing such a gift in a form of penetration into other people’s inner thoughts. One day, at the beginning of the foundation, Rosa heard these words from Jesus in answer to her wish to be of some use to the souls that were under her care:

Each time you will need to see into and penetrate certain hearts, you will see them like this… You will distinguish clearly the good from the bad; I will let you feel abhorrence when these will have indecent ideas against chastity… As regards false devotion, you will have special light so as to discern it well…

This shows the extraordinary intuitive capacity of the Servant of God. In the Memorie, she herself seems to wonder in observing how clearly she is able to see into the other people’s inner thoughts and their reactions. In 1873 she wrote:

I see in the sisters the slightest thing that goes on inside them, so much so that I say nothing, or else they would notice too much.

And yet, they were really aware; many of them were convinced that the Mother could read their consciences. There is no need of putting into notice that the repeated experience of this gift placed the Servant of God in a completely personal perspective, in the human context in which her life was unfolding. 4. Predictions of future events

Even the gift of prophecy is among the charisms which are at the service of the faithful. Moreover in the traditional scheme of signs required for the canonization of a Servant of God, there was this gift, conceived as superior knowledge of hidden things or as annunciation of future things. Today little importance is given to such a sign of holiness, if not for other reasons, for the difficulty of verifying the real supernatural nature of the prophetic visions. Saint John Bosco wrote his memoirs at the same time of Mother Rosa. Among other charisms granted to him by the Lord for the benefit of the souls, were his dreams and prophecies, the content of which created real problems of interpretation. In this area, it is particularly difficult to distinguish between predictions or personal presages and Introduction divine revelation. In most cases, it is not clear that prophetic visions have a purpose in the plan of God.

Rosa Gattorno was aware of the risk of ascribing to God what does not belong to God. In August 1885 she wrote:

How many prophesies they say and write to me, but until now its only one which is becoming true. When Sister Anne del

Salvatore was alive, I experienced many and all true… But for many others of these prophets and prophetesses, I see that my

God does not allow; them to tell me things the way I know they are. Oh, how easy it is to be mistaken! When we want to put our things in God’s affairs, then all becomes imperfect.

As we pointed out in the book Spiritual Portrait of Rosa Gattorno (p. 98), some of the predictions of Mother Rosa were confirmed by some witnesses, concretely by the notes added to the letters of the Servant of God, by the Princess of Fitalia. Others, instead, do not seem to have divine origin. These were political events regarding the prophecy on the fall of Rome, the devastation of Paris, the impending death of Pope Leo XIII (announced in 1885) after which the inauspicious election of his successor and that of a “holy pope” would take place. This does not affect at all her sincerity. 5. The Memorie are not a biographical diary

Rosa Gattorno entrusts to the paper what her spirit is living. The exterior events, even those regarding her person, are registered only in so far as they arise in her profound spiritual effects. It surprises us that certain very important events regarding her person are not even mentioned; for example, the news about the death of her father on January 17, 1874 and that of her mother on December 18, 1882.

In conclusion, for a correct and profitable reading of the Memoirs of Rosa Gattorno there is need of being in tune with the tension of her spirit, enlightened and guided by faith, with the richness of the mystical experience, with her ultra-human perspective of common events. The Memorie are as a very sensible registration of the repercussions alternated in her spirit about everything regarding God’s interests, centered in the Work, the leadership of which was entrusted to her care. Her’s is a story of suffering and love lived by a heart open to God and for God to human beings.

The secret message of the Memoirs

This dialogue with herself and with the Supreme Good, though, without an explicit addressee and prolonged for almost 25 years, has the value of being a living witness, which after a century still speaks for us today, that of an exceptional experience of God’s success in a soul, an itinerary strewn with interior battles, fears, and inexpressible tortures when she experienced the abandonment of her beloved Good, and at the same time of efforts to carry on (in the midst of misunderstandings, oppositions and bitterness) the Work for which she became Foundress only out of obedience to the representatives of God.

When she filled her notebooks, after the toil of the day at the service of the Work of God, in the shelter of her room, certainly she did not have in mind her dear Daughters of Saint Anne, present or future addressees. But she warmly kept them present. Moreover, many of her reflections in-between mystical raptures, become teachings of great importance at present, for example, when she speaks of spiritual direction, of criteria to discern the true gifts of God in prayer, the snares of pride, one’s own will, of true humility; not to mention of her observations on the occasions of her visits in the houses and, above all, of her enlightened talks to the sisters, profound and at the same time practical.

In the case of Rosa Gattorno, as for many saints of exceptional life, we could use the saying: “Holiness is to be admired not to be imitated.” Certainly her dietetics of Introduction physical flagellation, the sensible manifestations of her fervor of love, her participation in the suffering of Christ, and that night mess of ghosts, beasts and fatigue do not belong to the normal track of the life of perfection.

But there is much to be imitated in the totality and faithfulness of a love which does not know laxity, a love that finds full expressions of tenderness, always original and not learned: Being of my life, my only Good, my life, object of my life, my All, my Love, pasture of all my delights, sweetness without compare… There is much to be imitated in her permanent union with her supreme Good, which is not an exercise of prayer limited to determined hours or ways but a constant breathing in God… There is much to be imitated in that faith-trust in the providential love of God the Father who comes to help in the urgent needs in a miraculous way, who even settles the annual budget, a secret which she does not want to reveal even to the apostolic visitor… There is much to be imitated in her prompt charity with the sick or afflicted sisters, with the poor in the hospitals, with the sinners… Finally there is much to be learned in that deep of serenity and unchanging joy, not only in the moments of communications of love in which she repeats: “The joy I feel is without compare,” but also in the midst of corporal sufferings and the torments of her spirit. Rosa Gattorno is a soul basically happy. This depth of peace should be picked up from all the events of the phase of the binomial suffering-love. For the person who knows how to discover this guiding line, the pages of the Memoirs can be fascinating.

THE PRESENT EDITION a) Disposition of the text

The original manuscripts of the Memorie were delivered at the death of the Servant of God to Monsignor Granito Pingatelli di Belmonte, future Cardinal, who after examining them carefully, to see if there was anything which could create difficulty in case of a process of canonization, handed them back with other writings to the Daughters of Saint Anne (Summarium, p. 5f). The two big reports, to which we gave the title autobiography, were written in five paper form tied in the respective booklets. All the other Memoirs are found in simple exercise books (of secular use) of different sizes.

In the occasion of the official examination of the censors, designated by the Sacred Congregation of the Rites of the time, the exercise books – 39 in all – were paged and grouped in 16 booklets. This is the classification kept in the Archive of the Institute. A small pocket-able exercise book, where the Foundress used to note down her observations and a memorandum of her visits to the houses, was added.

Among many exercise books, in the midst of which loose papers of doubtful date are not missing, it is possible that some have been lost; this could explain certain important gaps found in some years.

Beyond the originals, the Archive has double copies, (manuscript and typewritten) of all the exercise books (Collocation in AFSA –A. 331-33).

In planning the edition, two solutions were offered. The simplest would have been that of reproducing the booklets and the note books the way they are found. But, examining the manuscripts, it was verified that Mother Rosa does not dedicate an exercise book per year, but when she fills an exercise book she continues to write in another; moreover many times she utilizes the papers, which remained empty at the end of an exercise book, for the purpose of inserting Introduction some forgotten things. Putting in order the series of the exercise books, attention has not always been made to the chronological succession. Therefore following this track would result in a confused publication, difficult in reading and little consistent with the aim of the content itself.

For this reason, we opted for an arrangement of all the contents in two big sections and four appendices.

SECTION I. AUTOBIOGRAPICAL REPORT. Five in all: two copies written retrospectively within the years of 1874 to1878 and three more brief ones. comprise the dated Memorie, not very accurate in the first years, more accurate in the last years, but with the possibility of arranging them in the corresponding year. These are dated from 1872-1894. This chronological grouping, in addition of making the reading easier, will help to locate the personal experiences of the Foundress in the historical context in which she wrote them. Regarding the years 1892-1896. HOUSES. These notes start in 1881 and end in 1890. SISTERS. They comprise ten years: 1888-1898.

Foreseeing the necessary comparisons of a text with the original, at the beginning of every year and in passing to a new exercise book, we brought accurately the number of the respective booklet keeping the paging added to the manuscript. This is reproduced even at the edge of every page in print following the graphic sign of two parallel lines (//).

To do the reading easier, subtitles extrapolated from the contents of the text, in a form similar to that used in the edition of the book Travagli e Conforti, have been introduced.

Finally, for an arrangement in the biographical time and space, it seemed very useful to place at the beginning the chronology of the life of Rosa Gattorno, accurately compiled by Sister Anne Roberta Frati. b) Criteria adopted for the transcription

The handwriting of Mother Rosa is uniform, more accurate and connected in the first years and more loose in the last years, but always clear enough for an accurate reading. Neglected instead is the orthography and, more than this, the punctuation. Moreover, forced to write at night, taking away the time of rest, under the pressure of different feelings which accumulate in her spirit, Mother Rosa does not care about the grammatical structure of the time. She interrupts to relieve her feelings with an exclamation, an act of love… She then skips a verb, an adjective, a particle…

For this edition a criterion of paleographic faithfulness might have been followed, in which case it might be enough to reproduce a typewritten copy. But it is preferable to offer a readable and clear text, still respecting to the maximum the original that is the thought of the Servant of God.

Therefore we tried to complete the incomplete phrases, adding the word that she probably had in mind. Instead the items which seemed unnecessary are removed. When the meaning is confusing an attempt has been made to be close to the thought of Mother Rosa in footnotes.

Among the personal parenthesis to be noted is the adversative conjunction – “But!” It is used very often as a final interjection, to show doubt or uncertainty. Introduction

By Sr. A. Roberta Frati The goal of the present chronology is to make known the journey accomplished by Mother Anne Rosa Gattorno. Therefore, it has been extracted mainly from her letters and integrated with events commonly known in addition to the diary of Sister A. Celsa Speranza which sometimes has been found incorrect. In cases of uncertainty other documents, letters which were received and telegrams have been consulted. Small news and thoughts have not been collected because though they enrich the chronology, they would prolong excessively the time of writing out the same. In reading and using the chronology one needs to keep in mind some objective problems such as the grammatical and syntax errors made by Mother Rosa in writing and the difficulty of interpreting some dates. Such problems and the particular style of writing make this chronology more imperfect, incomplete and susceptible therefore to corrections.

INTRODUCTION

CHRONOLOGY

FIRST REPORT EXPERIENCES OF THE YEARS 1870 - 1874 MS Booklet 1, Part I, pp. 1- 196 When Mother Rosa, after the first events as Foundress from 1867 to1868, felt the thrust of putting into writing the secret dimension of her life, which took place between God and herself; she saw refreshing in her memory and in her heart the birth of many experiences, which had already became constituent of her everyday living in God and for God. She remembered the new rhythm of piety and apostolate which her life had undertaken, fruit of an increasingly intensive self-giving to her crucified Spouse. It was a love of someone who was converted, desiring only to express her faithfulness through the humiliation of repentance and the flagellation of the body. Her stay in Saint Francis of Albaro in the years 1861-1862 was a true relief for her spirit, which was increasingly opening to the enlightenment of the divine contemplation. It was also the beginning of particular mystical graces. The Suffering will become for Mother Rosa an essential demand of love. Her retrospective narration, actually relived, is every now and then interrupted to give space to the actual state of her soul while she writes. Having offered herself as a sacrifice through the three vows of chastity, poverty and obedience, she feels that her supreme Good fully commands her life. At a certain point she refrains from recalling about the years of Genoa to transmit the lived experiences after her relocation to Piacenza, where the sweet “room” would be for many years the only witness of her loving impulses, of her ecstasy, of her penances and of her struggles.

From the few chronological indications it can be deduced that since 1869 the spiritual notes were more frequent, almost a diary. In the last part of the booklet, there are indications of the day and month but not the year, while in the last pages we find experiences which correspond to the year 1874.

Therefore, we have divided the contents of this first report into three stages: the first, a retrospective type until 1866; the second, regarding the first years of the foundation in Piacenza; and the third, where some events are gathered placed between 1870 and 1874. 1. SPIRITUAL ITINERARY, THE YEARS OF GENOA (1857-1866)

MS 1.1- pp. 1-36

“As though I had entered another kind of life”

In the year 1857,* being free from all ties, I dedicated myself with greater fervor to pious works and visiting hospitals and the poor sick in their homes, offering them as much help as I could and serving them in every way. By the grace of God I realized that all my earthly affections were dissipating, nothing attracted me anymore; only my God was the pasture of my delights. The trials of my family were without compare. I poured them all out to the heart of my beloved Crucifix, for him alone. I continued to tell repeatedly to myself that all my sufferings were very little, because I had committed many sins. I could not remove certain little things, for living in the family this was not allowed. Oh, how I had to struggle!

In 1858 I vowed obedience and chastity; in regard to the latter I was not allowed to make a perpetual vow but only for a year. At the same time I took the rope of Saint Francis of Assisi1 and had much desire of afflicting this miserable beast of a body and, // if I could be allowed, I would have slaughtered it; I hated it so much for being so disgraceful.

I received great graces from the Blessed Virgin Mary.

During the novena of Our Lady of the Vines, while the Blessed Sacrament was exposed for the benediction, I saw the living blood which seemed to be flowing in the most Holy

Host. What I felt at this sight I cannot express: a union, a fire that devoured me! But stupid as I am, I paid no heed, and thought it a common thing. Oh, how great is the goodness of my Jesus! In the novena of the Immaculate - it was not yet a year since I took the vow of chastity – I was allowed to make perpetual vow of chastity, poverty and obedience. I placed everything at Mary’s feet, for her to give all this to my good

Jesus and I asked him to accept me as his bride. Oh, what I felt! As though I had entered another kind of life and I did not know if I was alive or who was living for me. The trials of my family were without compare, but clutching my Good //

I would repeat: Oh, my sins deserve worse than hell itself; and I shall willingly go there to feel the pain, as long as you lead me there holding me close and tight! You alone are my heaven. And I wept a lot for having offended him.

Within the bounds of obedience I increased my penances as much as I could and I felt such pleasure in oppressing this disgraceful body that I cannot explain how much consolation

I was feeling.

In the novena of Our Lady of theVines in 1859, I had deep experiences of consolation, union with the Good, beautiful visions and interior words. I would have remained the whole day if my duties could allow it.

These consolations were strengthening me in such a way that if I had to face any trouble I would not be distressed. I was feeling such a balanced cheerfulness that I seemed the happiest creature of this earth, and I made all the others believe, this because I said nothing, while the trials were many. During the novena // of the Redeemer I had a permission to increase the penances. I put on a bodice with iron points stitched into it, and a big chain on the legs, arms, feet, and head. I also fasted: on the eve a little bread and a little water for the whole day. Yet I was feeling my strength increasing, as if those penances and the discipline to bleeding were my great nourishments.

However, at the eve, while I was expecting great consolations, because I got used to receiving them, especially on feast days, instead I was arid. Alas, what will become of me? Perhaps I have done something bad, and so my Good has gone away. What have I done? And I was very sad. I did not know where to find peace. Who knows how much I lost because I had not yet learnt how to fight under the banner of the Holy Cross, so delightful and dear. But what a lot of mistakes one makes as a beginner! But soon I went to my director, who calmed me and assured me that there was nothing wrong, and ordered me to be serene. // This happens to those souls who like to stay on Tabor.2 Oh, dear Jesus! Yes, let us love Calvary and in suffering we shall discover its delights; by getting closer to the object of our love, suffering becomes the soothing balm that we crave.

The sins crossed out by the Blood of the Redeemer

In the caresses he often gave me, he was giving me something of his own gifts, such as that of meditation; just after Holy Communion, for instance, clinging to my Good, it was more a contemplation than a meditation, because I would get into one of his wounds and stay there for hours, forgetting that I was alive, and the union kept growing inside me. At other times I was absorbed, and as in a dialogue, I would go off with my Jesus. He taught me many things. For a long time, at the end of this dialogue, he was showing me two books, which were held by two angels. One was very beautiful and not very thick. There was a list of names, and then a list of saints. At the end of the list there was my name written very visibly, and then: Saint. In the other book, that was thick, there were my sins; more than half were written and all were crossed out with the Blood of my dear Redeemer and, at the end of the list, again as // above, my name and then: Saint.

Oh, what I experienced! A union, an indescribable joy, and, if my Good delayed to show me, soon I turned to the Eternal

Father that he may allow me to see them and he granted me the vision. Oh, suffering!

Once I saw them covered by a black veil; what I felt I couldn’t express. I wept and wept so much that I would destroy myself by weeping because I felt as if I had lost everything. The comfort I experienced was such that no fear of not being forgiven by my Good could seize me. After weeping at length the veil was removed from them. My

Eternal Father, for pity’s sake, give me all the pains that you wish, but never such a vision, which I continue to see. Oh, my Love! I do not deserve your graces, because I am disgraceful, but I love you!

The crown of thorns, presage of struggles and sufferings

Now, another thing is added, which I see placed over the books, now a palm, and now a beautiful crown. Oh, how beautiful! And now a crown of thorns, which // I rejoiced to have. Oh, poor sinner! Oh, goodness of God the Father!

Who would fail to destroy themselves for this dear Father?

Giving oneself to him is truly nothing in comparison with such an immensity of greatness. Oh, what boundless goodness! The desire of the crown of thorns was so much that I concealed it in holy meditation and decided on Thursdays to pause and meditate upon it.

One day after Holy Communion, I saw two angels approaching me bearing a crown of thorns which looked like that of my Beloved; it had one particularly long thorn, they drew near to place it on my head and I was desperate to feel it set upon me, although the thorns were very sharp. My desire to suffer was great, my pleasure was immense. Oh, how happy I would have been if they had left me with it for ever! But no, I only managed to obtain permission to wear one just like it on Thursday and Friday nights. The enemy began to fight with me and gave me such a blow right on my forehead that one of the thorns of the crown I was wearing pierced me // strongly and my forehead swelled. Oh, what a fear to be noticed by! My hair stood on end! In this way, he tormented me with temptations, sometimes they were so strong that I needed the strength which my Jesus gave me to resist. In my mind I tried to escape in the wound where I hid myself that day by following obedience, because the one who was directing me was telling me not to worry about and to feel not the sorrow. This order was so hard and was giving me much pain because, at least when I was attacked, I could not avoid feeling pain and suffering, always for fear of displeasing my Good. And how could I be cheerful, as he commanded me? I made every possible effort as much as I could so as to lose not my obedience. It was a strong battle.

Franciscan Tertiary

In 1861, I was clothed with the Franciscan habit as the friars. I had the same material given from the same people with a big rope and the skull on one side; I was wearing it day and night. It gave me much pain, because on the outside I was wearing the usual lay dresses.

I went to the countryside with the family and I was very sick, // a threat of tuberculosis. In this way, I was not able to meet my director and confessed rarely, since this was what he ordered me, but I was tormented by diabolic suggestions. I had only the strength that Jesus provided me with, that of nourishing me everyday with the heavenly bread. I confessed, when it pleased my Good, and that day I had a bit of peace, or I could feel little bit of relief.

In the novena of Our Lady of Carmel, I had terrible battles and an abyss of tribulations; and what made me suffer much were the diabolic suggestions, the temptations and what the ugly monster did to me; why show me that I will never have the grace that Jesus loves me? Oh, pains! I saw the abyss of my sins and finally the curses that seemed to me to have been pronounced, while in this way anger assailed me which I never knew before. Oh, suffering!

Mary, my dear Mother, came to my help with much love granting me great graces. Mary! The day of 16 July, 1861, while the Venerable, Holy Host was exposed, I saw an approaching globe of fire and it stayed close to the same // for sometime. On 21of the same month, while I was giving thanks for Holy Communion, oh, what “Ceppinello” the ugly one did to me! It showed me all kinds of tribulations:

that I did things that displeased Jesus and therefore I was unworthy to receive him and having received him … But when they reached a certain point at which I was not able to bear them anymore, my Good took away everything and I was left in perfect peace. Only after sometime I felt like weeping. “Oh, my sins,” I said.

On 17 September, I was assailed by horrible diabolic suggestions; the fight was so frightful and for that I was upset, but I was very calm and so united with my God that I did not remember having had such horrible fighting, but only in my mind. I had never been tormented by other things, never, as if my Good had always caressed me. Oh, the next day, what a beautiful day! I had my Beloved close to me.

Oh, what I felt! Though I did not see him anymore, since he had gone, I would never cease to stay as someone in prayer or, rather, not “praying” // but tasting whatever her Beloved had said.

But I had to be deprived even of this, because, in that church my mother was with me and she waited for me.

Therefore, I had to go home, I threw myself to the ground and, clutching my Crucifix, I gave vent… in this way I remained united with him the whole day. I did not stay always in my room but stayed at my duties as usual, often making spiritual aspirations. My Love, consume me!

Everything is yours. Is it true, my Love? - I asked him because, if there is something which does not please you and does not belong to you, oh, tell me, that I will say as my father, Francis, that if he had something which did not belong to God, he would remove it quickly.3 Oh, my Love, and, in my case, I would burn it!

Vision of the Blood of the Redeemer

One day, in the countryside in a square, I was sitting on the ground with a little cushion under me, reciting the Office of the Blessed Virgin. Oh! I saw my Jesus next to me with his hands bound behind him. // Oh, what I felt! Oh, my Love, only you could describe the effect your visit had on me: strength to suffer more and resignation to your divine will.

Oh, my Love! When I had finished reciting the Office, I thanked my Good for showing such favor to a miserable sinner, a disgusting worm of the earth, but it is not I who am living, it is my Jesus who lives in me.4 Not satisfied, I went to church to thank him, though it was far and I had no good health and it was painful to walk, but my Good consoled me more. They were about to give the Benediction and the Blessed Sacrament was exposed. I saw the most precious Blood of my Good, and what effect did it have on me? Oh, my Love! You alone could tell what was being wrought out within me. I remained in ecstasy and I did not know, I could no longer say anything and all is little and nothing can be said to the merciful God by a poor, ignorant creature. After a long time I turned to my Father Francis and to all the seraphim and cherubim to // sing a hymn of thanksgiving for me to my God. On 24 September, I made profession in the Third

Order of St. Francis and chose this good Father as my advocate and the patron of my soul.5

Another day, while the Venerable Sacrament was exposed, I saw the face of my Redeemer. Oh, how beautiful it was! How much joy! Oh, my Love! He was so bright that I do not know how to explain his light and beauty and I felt all inflamed by that object that consumed me. Oh, when will the day come when in such a fine moment, you will consume me, my Good?

Temptations and interior afflictions

Some days have passed, in which I am deprived of such beautiful visions, but I feel peace and stillness of spirit. When the peace has ended, I found myself in the most terrible state of anguish, battled by strong thoughts, horrible figures in the mind; and then the diabolic suggestions that tortured me.

Oh! How I desired that it had struck me. The blows do not cause me as much pain as the cruel thoughts and the temptations. Patience! You, who are my Master, my dear

Love, my Jesus have // mercy on me. I have no one to ask for opinion and advice; you have taken away everything from me; I do not have but you, o my Spouse, and under your feet

I place everything; unbind this snare from my mind. Oh, my Father, you well know which point my affliction has reached;

I can resist no more.

This state increasingly grew because I was deprived of the caresses that I frequently received; I was always tormented because I feared of having caused them. I pleaded my Beloved that he may give me light to know what did not please him or if I missed in some thing. Oh, pains, how strong you are! Mortifications and pains increased and I did not know what to do, I would have butchered myself, if obedience would have allowed me. Patience! Battling in this way I went where my Good was exposed and, after a moment of calm there, I saw in the Holy Host the precious blood; always, as usual, I saw with the physical eyes // and for two days I saw it, but always one different from the other. Oh, sanctifying balm! I would willingly, languishingly remain, gazing and contemplating you.

Another morning I asked the Eternal Father to give me or rather to increase my cross and, if I had to struggle to drag it, I would carry it on the chest and not on the shoulders, because I was not worthy to carry it. I saw one very big that was carried by two angels and they were handing it to me; it had the three nails fixed on it. Oh, what happiness I felt! Oh, my Father, may I die on it! Afterwards, I had temptations and the enemy came with new assaults to attack me; the fight was such that I remained without strength. It came with anger but my Beloved fortified me with his strength in order to resist.

On the day of the Immaculate Conception, I added to my vows that of poverty, which I did not yet make because I was not allowed. Oh, holy poverty, much loved by my Spouse, it was so right that I even // loved it! Mary, most holy, teach me to carry out this poverty as my dear Jesus, your beloved Son, desires. Saint Francis, you my advocate, teach me to overcome even the least human consideration and reach the highest perfection.

I was again under tribulations, the most horrible there could be. Patience! Oh, how sweet, to suffer for the love of Jesus, deprived of any consolation! Oh, how they become increasingly rare! But my Good comforted me again, because after the thanksgiving – since the Blessed was exposed – I saw the blood in the Host; it mingled with his holy flesh, so clearly was it revealed to me! Oh, happy moments, if they could be more! But I know it is only Calvary, the sure mountain that I will stop on. Oh, my Love, you are my strength, my life.6

Penitences that give health

I fell ill and, because I did not want to say what I had, I always dragged myself to my feet, but with great struggle.

The pain I felt was // without compare but, not to be forced to reveal what I was feeling, I tried to be seen laughing. In this way they all thought that it was a spiritual sickness that reduced me to that state, because I was very thin, so weak that they said I frightened them. Someone said: “It is the strange kind of life she is leading.” Others said: “She does not eat.” My family was angry with the confessor and wanted to complain, because he allowed me things which were not good for my health. They made many arguments and suppositions, but no one knew the least thing, no one. One of the house women, who at night was going out with me to visit someone gravely sick, knew but never spoke. Oh, what graces my Good granted me! At night, after midnight, we were two women alone on the streets and never met anyone who could frighten us!

Therefore, the pain increased and I thanked my Beloved who, // provided me with such sweet food of suffering. moreover, he frightened me because // when I told him what Satan was doing to me, he did not understand and he wanted to exorcize me. It should be noted that this was the first grace I asked of my Love: that is, never to allow an earthly creature to be aware that I have the least thing capable to be believed on as good; in a word, that everything should remain hidden to the eyes of the people. I repeated to my Good: Do you want other penances? Tell me and give me strength to bear them. Oh, my Beloved! I do not live anymore; it is you who live for me in all that belongs to me. //

The Crucifix stuck in her chest

During the novena of the Saviour, I had very strong pains in my hands, feet and side. Yearning for penances

Oh, my Love! I do not know how to express what I experience in my continuous fasting of 24 hours. Oh, my Beloved, you could say it, you who granted me the strength and the consolation that I feel! If it was not for obedience, I would not need to // take that piece of bread, because I was nourished so much that I could not express it. Loaded with penances, I kept free only my hands and my face. On Sunday, after the birth of my Saviour, I was in ecstasy; but, still because my Good would never allow it. This was what he promised, but it was not like that when I remained alone in my room. Oh, sweet Love; how many raptures! Oh, beautiful illustrations! With much freedom, I abandoned myself to union with my Good, while outside I was always distracted. In this way, sometimes, in aridity, I try to meditate and I am as a trunk; then I turn to Mary, // in the immense pain she suffered when Jesus went to greet her and told her that he was leaving in order to be crucified for us wicked mortals and me, who is the worst of all, for I, made him suffer. Coming to myself, I felt as downcast as though I had been weeping bitterly and, an inner grief, lingered with regard to what I had been given to see.

My pain was so deep that for a long time I did not cease to continue a kind of sobbing, the pain was stronger than words can say.

Vision of the day of Easter Resurrection

On the day of Easter (of resurrection), oh, what I ever felt! I enjoyed the Feast that was taking place in heaven. Every choir had its own melody; with different sounds all passed to give homage to my Beloved, who, beautiful beyond any telling, was seated at the right hand of the Father. At a certain moment, I saw only one person, as if indicating to me God, one in three persons. Oh, what a beautiful illustrations! Finally I saw a choir and it was of the holy Fathers who were in the light of God. What did I feel and understand! It seemed as if my mind was absorbed in great and inconceivable things: the interwoven crowns and the angels. Oh, Love, why do you not show a bit of this to the non-believers?

Recovered, I paused in prayer but was always absorbed: Oh, my dearest Love, remember your sufferings and why you suffered. Ah, powerful God, for that suffering, pour upon the one who loves you the burning fire, // so that she may be consumed by your love, because I am craving for it. You satisfied the crowds and would you refuse to the one who lives only for you a sip of your Spirit? Lord, oh, what a thirst! My Good, you quenched a Samaritan woman; ah, pity, may my burning thirst move you! Oh, Love, the fire of your love is my only nourishment and, when I go to convert the sinners, may my words be very effective to convert the whole world. I suffer too much when I see you offended. Oh, my Good, what thirst I feel to give my life for them and, in this way, like the martyrs, to be put at the stake for you! Oh, fire without end, for I will never be quenched!

I saw such beautiful feast in heaven and the Sovereign

Mary at the right hand of God… Oh, what ever I understood!

And how can I express it, if I am an ignorant? Ah, Mary, darling Mother, remember this poor creature, who, here below is immersed in the shadows, because you keep me with you very briefly and then I return in this // miserable earth, where I find everything bad and rotten. Oh Mary! For the joy that you feel today, break the chains of this miserable creature.

Ah, listen to me, do not delay anymore to take me out of these painful snares and give me only your love.

May my life always be toiling and suffering for Jesus. Oh, may my iniquity allow nothing, because I am disgraceful. Ah, make yourself my teacher and teach me to do penance to make me less unpleasant to my dear Jesus and satisfy so may debts contracted through my failings. Oh, Holy Spirit, joy of hearts, why do you not, with the spark of your love, revive, burn, consume and destroy all the earthly affections, and let only the fire of your love remain unquenchable?

I saw the Eternal Father smiling; he was showing me an empty place and then Mary, with the Child, my Jesus, in her arms, in the act of holding him out to me; and it seemed to me that there was another person close to me. My Eternal Father made me understand many things, but forbade // me to write them down. I will only say that at the end he told me that he would protect me in a particular way in the battles we would have to bear, and likewise in those in which we are currently involved, and not to doubt anything regarding the punishment by the epidemic that would come; that I should not doubt, since he would protect not only me but also all those who will be with me and my relatives. He assigned me to give them a linen cloth soaked in his oil, that was blessed by the Eternal Father. They were to wear it always, and he told me to assure them that nothing bad would happen to them; in fact that was what happened.9

Vision on the eve of All the Saints (31 October 1866)

Oh, will I be able to describe what I saw and felt on the eve of All the Saints in this year of 1866! Oh, my Love, I am too ignorant to be able to find useful phrases in order to make a correct narration. Not at all! Can a human pen make the description of paradise? With your help, oh my Love, I will try to put something on this paper.

At half past three I felt a strong anxiety gripping me and something that enraptured me; the worry was increasing // and the rapture was increasingly growing; I felt I was dying. I was feeling that something had to happen within me. Oh, Love! When I was fully absorbed in God, I rejoiced: Oh, sweetness without compare! I saw the feast that was being prepared in heaven, oh, immense joy! The angels with garlands and melodies were encircling all the saints who had greater splendor; the souls of paradise were competing to fete their advocates. Oh, paradise, how beautiful you are! Your joys and your feasts make me die! Oh, when will be that blessed day, when freed from this miserable humanity, I will come to embrace you, my Love, to be with you for eternity!

The sight of my Good was ever before me, very beautiful: those rays, the light, the beauty. At the end I was always feeling certain things, as if I was not yet fully loosened from the vision of the rapture; I do not know. And I was enraptured again, I found myself close to the side of my Beloved, what did I feel! // I cannot describe it. The feeling of being pressed closely against the volcano of love… Oh, how painful life seems to me! Oh, my dear Beloved, let me abide with you and not to return to this miserable earth! Oh, painful exile, when will it finish? But soon I began saying: No, I live in order to suffer! Oh, my dear Beloved, forgive me if I thirst to be removed from this valley; but no, I repeat, suffering! It is exquisite, the honey of your sweetness, how can I fail to hunger for it? I suffer and feel that this miserable body twists and struggles, but no, dear Jesus, with your help I will be firm on the cross, suffering and languishing for you.

Yes, now I can say I have one, but I will never say:

Enough! My Good, I will only say that I suffer much. The suffering is so much that I feel no life at all; it seems to me like living always in a continuous anguish. Oh, my Beloved, your love // consumes me; I feel a devouring flame that burns me and consumes me, a continuous spasm that I can bear no longer. I do not suffer, because it is quite delicious; the joy I feel is incomparable. But what comes to me is the fear that it might disappear, as someone who holds a great treasure. I thought it is a useless comparison. I fear losing it. Oh, what pain I feel at the mere thought, that I might inadvertently disgust him; if I could feel the pains; this would be enough to take my life away.

“My sweet Love! If human beings knew you…”

For pity’s sake, satiate me with your love! Oh, why do I not always remain before your ciborium where, my Delight, you are enclosed? What are five or six hours a day? Nothing!

Let me remain close to you without moving anymore; let me search for nothing; let only what I see be my pasture. Oh, only you, my Love, as you desire. Oh, light of my eyes, my sweet Love! If people knew you, they would certainly leave

// everything and come to the foot of your altar to enjoy your delights.

But how can I make them understand me? Oh, what a torment it is for me and it will be the same for all those who love you when they see you offended. I feel a cruel thought within me, stronger than myself. The sight of many faithful and some religious, who are cold towards you, is not less cruel. Ah, accept my dear Jesus, that my blood may be poured to expiate such enormous mistreatments and contempt.

Oh, yes, sometimes I will be scolded for my grumbling, but I can not bear it. I would be very happy if for you, my Good, I could receive blows; I would be happy. I would like to do many things to amend some of those failures. Not at all! I have nothing good and, when I look at myself I find nothing, only misery and filthiness. // Seeing my nothingness and my deformities, I cover my face and I weep about my misery and the wickedness I have committed.

Temptations: torments for remoteness of God

I was very strongly assailed by diabolic suggestions and temptations of every kind. Only those against chastity, I never experienced, but rather against faith and against my Good: the sight that there was nothing else for me but an abyss where I could be swallowed. While I was fighting in this way, I felt something approaching; at a certain moment I saw a big serpent with an open mouth ready to bite me; I remained motionless looking at it. I turned to my Mother Mary: My Mother, save me; Hail Mary! And it ran away. It left me very frightened, but I continued to pray to the Blessed Virgin Mary, because I was in the novena of the Immaculate. On the day of her Feast, I received many gifts. Oh, Mary!

In my penances there was one which pleased // my Good; every time it gave me fire that burned and it was so very strong that I fainted. Oh, my Love, what did you do to make me feel in this heart of yours! Oh, if human beings could understand what I’ve experienced, certainly they would not hesitate for a minute to give up those affections which wither quickly and fall in a breath. Everything is rotten and heavier than a piece of bacon; only your love increases every day or, rather, it has no end.

4th September: I was tossed about by a stormy sea of tribulations and my laments were not heard. A thought came to me: “Did you not wish to suffer?” Oh, yes, I replied. And I abandoned myself totally to this suffering. I tried to absorb it all with resignation, giving myself up entirely to the Father’s will. But all the while my sufferings grew stronger, and I cried: Help! Mercy! I prayed to Mary, but she did not show herself. Oh, whatever have I done to you? I prayed to St. Joseph and to St. Francis, my Father; not even they were moved by pity. But the greatest pain of all was to see the Father and Jesus so immobile, one with a look of indifference and the other with a kind of disdain. Oh, what have I done to you, Being of my life? Have pity on me! Increase the pain as much as you want but do not show me yourself disdained.

Oh, the pain was too much; it made me faint.

In this way the diabolic suggestions grew stronger; there

Satan said to me: “They have all abandoned you! Turn to me.” Oh, ugly monster! I said. But it did not stop insisting with infernal cunning that gave me unbearable torments.

What sufferings, what battles, my God! //

Weeping I said: My Father, allow me to shed these tears at your feet; my Love, for the pain you underwent in Golgotha when you were abandoned, grant me and accept that I may be consumed at your feet, for in this way, if you give me a bit of life, I will remain… Though you do not want to listen to me, I will never go away and will not cease weeping until I will have the strength to wet your wounds with my tears. Mary, have pity on this wretched creature of yours; tell me what I did to disgust my Good, the Being of my life. Experience in climbing the Holy Stairs in Rome.

The stigmata

There was nothing helpful to obtain a comfort, a help in such terrible pains. Only on the eve of Christmas, was I relieved; I was absorbed in God and I received beautiful explanations and knowledge in all matters: how to behave in the cruel events // and how to deal with people. Oh, what beautiful lessons accompanied by a fire that was consuming me and this continued until after the first of the year. I remember that it was the eve of the circumcision; I was traveling and all night long I was constantly with Jesus and Mary, who were visibly close to me and enabled me to master what was to happen to me. I had new explanations and other gifts. They showed me what would happen to me. The increasing of the fire which never ceased.

There are moments in which I seem to be consumed and, if I would not be raised up, when it is very strong and for a very long time, I could not live. Oh, sweet death in such delicious fire, how willingly would I be destroyed by that flame. Oh, what I felt that night!

I went to climb the Holy Stairs in Rome; I was enraptured with my God, so united with my Beloved that I was no longer alive. I felt great consolations. I was struck with pains in my hands and feet // and heart; as I recovered, all my veins seemed to be open; what I felt was such that I could not express it.

When I had recovered my senses, I found my strength and went home. I immediately tried to lie down with the hope of finding some relief. Not at all! My hopes were in vain. After some minutes, the fire increased so much that it seemed to consume me. My love came closer and caressed me; the pains in my hands, feet and heart increased and I felt that I was dying. It seemed to me that I was within a furnace and I remained in ecstasy for a long time.

I saw beautiful things; he told me things that I had longed to know; he gave me explanations; he fortified me with certain things so that, when I came to myself, I felt stronger and the pains in my feet, hands and heart were less. In this state of inebriation, I was turning over in my mind all that I had seen and enjoyed; thus I stayed for at least two hours. //

The following day I felt the same way. Oh, the fear of being discovered by people kept me always fearing, though I did not doubt what my Good promised me - that never a human creature would discover it. My Good - I always said when I am alone, do with me what you want: burn me, consume me, destroy me but let no one discover it. But what am I saying, my Good? Your promise can never fail.11

Presages on the fate of Rome and Paris

Another day he showed me how his Majesty was scorned and that there was nothing that could calm him. The Virgin Mary was praying and I was stricken with terror by the vision of the wide-scale destruction of two cities, one by fire, the other by war. Paris was destroyed by fire and Rome by war. The disaster was horrible: My Good, have pity on them! I offered myself as a victim so that he might shower it down all on me and that it might abate.12 I cannot describe how I suffered; I was so sorrowful that I could not give sign of life. It all caused me pain, gazing constantly at the sight of my God in the act of being severe and angry. //

In Rome, where I was, one morning I saw how Jesus left even the just ones in the dark, I prayed much, but I had always new visions. Now Jesus told me about having removed his grace and mercy from those people. One day, I pleaded with him more than usual that, for mercy’s sake, he may stop his punishment and I offered him a thousand things; it was useless. I still remained absorbed in him and saw the Eternal Father; beneath him was a black veil, which was spread all over Rome, and I saw my Beloved, with an unsheathed sword in an attitude of a very severe judge. Oh, what a pain! I went to the church, where the Blessed Sacrament was exposed, and prayed much. Within me I felt such a deep pain that I could not give a sign of life; I got nothing.

I had been warmly entrusted a superior with the thought that she could do much good if she recovered. I was seriously committed and, with much prayer, I resorted to my Good that // he may heal her. I knew that I was capable of nothing because I merited nothing, but the mercy and the charity of my Beloved compensated for my poverty. He told me that he would heal her but he wanted the washing of his wound with my blood and this I did by disciplining myself until bleeding.

Again he showed me the punishment of Rome and then I said to my Good: Ah, for charity’s sake, have mercy on these people! I prayed that for the prayers of the just souls in that city, he may become calm and forgive, stopping the punishment. No, he showed me the double heartedness and… Oh, my Love, the Pope! The Pope! Dear Pius IX!

Oh, he showed me, how much he loved him! He will have nothing, and in a meanwhile, he showed me a thousand other things, but all beautiful, that raised me from the sorrowful discouragement where I found myself in.

Vision on the day of Corpus Domini (1866)

Oh, if I could say what I saw and felt on the day of Corpus Domini! Oh, my Love, // what I felt the whole morning! After having reckoned on where the love of God reaches to, a God who gives himself to human beings, lowering himself down to us most unworthy creatures of the earth, I was then enraptured in the spirit and enjoyed a perfect union with my Good. Oh, Being of my living, I felt as though dying, your love agonizes me! I saw many good souls who, because of much fear, did not receive those graces which my Good kept ready for them. Their fear made them distrust God and they were always doubtful and perplexed; for this reason they were never able to have the sweet balsam of the love of Jesus. Oh, love him, and do not be afraid of the Beloved, but have fear of disgusting him.

The pain is strong and cannot be expressed, but the thought of mercy is without compare. A gaze to the tabernacle is enough to see what the loving Jesus did for us.

Oh, life // of my life! When I saw this, I was enraptured in him and saw the face of my God for a little while. It seemed to teach me to pray, and he gave me other cognitions. A strong fire inculcated within me, but new tribulations were added which tortured me; they were very strong. If I had not the strength of my God that sustained me, I would have truly been crushed by them. But my dear Mother Mary did not delay to comfort me, appearing to me with her dear beloved

Child. Oh, what comfort!

But the evil serpent, who never leaves me to live in peace, always brought me new torments; now he was striking – and this was painful- now as soon as I went to rest on an iron bed (I put boards over the iron; I spread over those other wood) I was tired and worn-out. I had only two hours for rest. Satan irritated me; it removed the iron boards // and, in a blow, everything went to the ground; a sound! Oh, what pain I felt, because in the morning they asked me whatever I was doing; and since it knew that this made me to suffer most, it amused itself in tormenting me with turmoil of every kind.

I was not able to tell this to my director, because, as I said, he already distressed me very much and wanted to exorcize me and asked the permission of the Archbishop. I pleaded with him much so that he might not do that and I turned to my Good; I beseeched him to tell me how I should behave and I was taught on this issue. In this way, little by little, I said nothing of what the monster was doing to me, which were things of every kind. But my Good had armed me with his strength and when it struck me, my…//

… and resignation to bear everything with much patience and that I bear everything with much consolation of the spirit. Many times I would like to turn to a wise priest, but Jesus did not want it and, in this way, I stay with the one he had assigned me.

The whole day from the church to the hospital

The day of circumcision, how I spent it completely with my Love! He appeared to me tiny; how beautiful! And he left me much peace and resignation in everything; and I felt that a very sublime Being was within me; he sustained me, guided me and gave me strength in the midst of cruel tribulations. I do not dwell in writing them, because I hand them over to my Good and I am not bothered. Oh, Love, you make me die and languish! Oh, blessed days! When I had a bit of freedom, I passed the whole day between the church and the hospital, near my dear sick, giving them my poor service.

On 2nd February, // while I was in contemplation in a church, what great things I felt! Oh, my poor soul, you are still tied to this stinking body; exiled and imprisoned in it, you must remain! Oh, if you could untie, it is certain that in a flight you could reach the infinite Being! And here, enraptured, I found myself close to the side of my Beloved;

what I felt!

After this, I remained in the presence of the Eternal

Father, who reached out his right hand to me; he was so resplendent that I do not know how to express it better; I could say everything. I saw paradise, one God in three and then, in a while, God alone in all its beauty. Oh, the pen of

St. Paul would be needed to describe these visions, I am not capable. The fire is such that it consumes me and, if it does not calm down a bit, I cannot live; at least I cannot do otherwise but exclaim at every moment: I cannot bear it anymore, I am burning!

The whole night I spent in continuous lament: I am dying, my Good, I am dying! These were two hours of sleep on the ground, without anything, but only a piece // of wood under my head; and yet it is my relief; but the ground warms quickly and the fire increases.

Only when I have afflictions and tribulations, then I feel relief because I feel this fire less. Oh, how I thirst to suffer, I feel no pain, because the thirst of suffering is without compare and it is sweet to suffer for the Beloved.

To suck the wounds of Jesus in those of the sick

On 7th February, something happened in the meditation which enraptured me and it was as though I was close to the wound on his back. Oh, my Love! Then I said: I will wash this wound with my tears and suck the humor. Oh! My Love, I was immediately overwhelmed by a flood of tears, and, as if I could suck that balm with my own mouth. I recovered and found myself full of strength, while before I had been worn out by my efforts for the sick and the poor whom I went to assist.

I felt almost like fainting when I returned to my poor room. But, for my Good, (whose word never // fails, because of the so little I do; he gives me so much) it was not enough to have given me the strength with that blessed balm. He also willed to grant me his vision, which has in such a strong way inebriated me; I do not find words to express myself. Oh, dear Jesus! In these days the fire is less burning for some time, but I find myself in such a way that I feel great pain, because I see how much misery is in me: no good, all rotten, my faults are all lined up before me. Oh, am I not an abyss of every iniquity? The pain of this sight is intolerable, agonizing more than can be said. Oh, my Love, use this miserable tool once to revive faith and for the conversion of sinners. Pleading in this way I stayed for long hours.

On Saturday, after three hours of meditation, the fire increased in me so much that I felt to breathe my last. // I would have cried out but I was afraid of being heard. Oh, I am dying! My Beloved, will it be perhaps this day that you will consume me? Oh, no, because immediately he showed me that I have long time to live and I said to him: My Love, tell me that you would like to extinguish my life with this fire! When I had recovered I went to the hospital, where I found utter happiness, for nothing discouraged me and nothing was repellent. Cleaning the wounds was the most pleasurable thing, for it seemed I was doing so for my Beloved Jesus. Many times I had to try to turn aside in order not to be enraptured by him and to abstain from kissing them, for I realized that the sick person was speaking. I also had to abstain from sucking the wounds, for fear that I might be found out and this is what I realized.13

The gift of discernment of hearts

One day, it happened that I was in the midst of evil people for the mission I had to do, gathering young girls for the First Holy Communion. They spoke // and said things which I did not understand at all; I was as though deaf and my head captured nothing.

Oh, what is happening to me? I asked to myself. What do

I have today, that I am not getting? I do not understand. Dear

Jesus, what is it all about? All these people speak and the other men reply yet I understand nothing. Almost frightened, I ran to a church and I said to my Good: Tell me, my Beloved, the thing that is going to happen to me? What is this happening to me?
